## Context / Problem
Clients authoring epic plans can repeat volatile graph metadata by stating the current number of children, and can add a redundant acceptance criterion requiring every child to close. The packaged plan-review author guide at `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` should steer them toward durable epic outcomes and decomposition instead; child closure is already enforced deterministically before parent completion as documented in `docs/llm-framework.md`.

## Approach
Add concise container-specific guidance to the canonical packaged guide: do not state the child count in an epic description, and do not add a separate acceptance criterion for all children being closed/completed. Rejected: changing plan-review or completion-verifier behavior, because the request concerns author guidance and the existing deterministic closure guard already supplies the invariant.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`: clarify durable epic description and acceptance-criteria guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar explain plan` tells clients not to include the number of children in an epic description; verified by rendering the packaged guide and reviewing the container guidance.
- [ ] `rebar explain plan` tells clients an epic needs no separate acceptance criterion stating that all children are closed/completed; verified by rendering the packaged guide and reviewing the container guidance.
- [ ] Existing guide packaging/rendering checks pass from the worktree virtualenv.
